notes: First real campaign (2026-10-28), CPU-feasible by design: full factorial = 2 augments x 2 lrs x 3 seeds = 12 runs of tiny-cnn (3 epochs, PneumoniaMNIST train n=4708, test n=624), executed as 3 rounds x 4 runs via the per_round budget cap. CI target is deliberately strict (0.005) so the full factorial completes; the Critic stops on budget exhaustion or when every cell CI meets the target. Wall-clock budget for the campaign process: 60 minutes. Dataset pre-seeded via curl (MD5-verified against the official MedMNIST checksum) because Python HTTP downloads are unreliable on this VM.
question: On PneumoniaMNIST, what drives test-accuracy variance more: augmentation, learning rate, or seed noise?
